execution.reason: Behavior and policy contracts establish RED first; the core utility follows; producer and frontier-consumer policy form a disjoint fork; evidence and invalidation then join both branches before integration verification.

tasks.title: Establish graph behavior and policy contracts
tasks.description: Tests capture graph invariants, frontier behavior, version compatibility, producer/consumer policy, evidence links, and read-only reporting before production changes.
acceptance_criteria: Behavior tests cover duplicate IDs, dangling dependency/conflict targets, self-edges, dependency cycles, status/pass coherence, and version-2 evidence rules.
Frontier tests cover dependency gating, running-task conflicts, one-sided conflict normalization, and file overlap.
Existing version-1 artifacts are valid fixtures and new version-2 evidence requirements are explicit.
Policy tests require canonical graph producers, dynamic frontier consumers, evidence links, conservative invalidation, and transient code neighborhoods.
The all-artifacts frontier test proves no write to .active or task artifacts.
tasks.expected_verification_state: Both commands exit non-zero only for the named unimplemented graph behavior and policy contracts.

tasks.title: Implement deterministic task-graph utility
tasks.description: A single dependency-free module validates versioned task graphs, computes conflict-free ready frontiers, and reports all artifact frontiers without mutation.
acceptance_criteria: The validate command emits deterministic machine-readable output and exits non-zero on structural errors.
The frontier command returns only pending nodes whose dependencies passed and which do not conflict with running nodes.
Declared conflicts are normalized as undirected and overlapping files prevent concurrent readiness.
Version-1 graphs remain readable; version-2 graphs enforce attempts and evidence references.
The --all artifact scan is report-only and never changes .active or graph files.
No package, extension, database, daemon, or second production module is introduced.
verification: for f in .pi/artifacts/*/tasks.json; do node --experimental-strip-types .pi/scripts/task-graph.ts validate "$f"; done

tasks.title: Make task producers graph-canonical
tasks.description: Create, plan, and lifecycle guidance emit or refine one version-2 tasks.json graph while treating displayed waves as derived views.
acceptance_criteria: New work emits version-2 task nodes with attempt and evidence_refs fields while preserving version-1 read compatibility.
tasks.json is named the only authoritative persisted work graph.
Plan node IDs match tasks.json and plan changes update the canonical graph.
Textual waves are explicitly derived snapshots and divergence is a stop condition.
The four-artifact lifecycle remains intact with no new canonical state file.

tasks.title: Execute the dynamic ready frontier
tasks.description: Ship, batch execution, and subagent guidance validate and repeatedly consume conflict-free ready frontiers with bounded transient code neighborhoods.
acceptance_criteria: Ship validates the canonical graph before execution and stops on graph errors or plan/task ID drift.
Ship computes a deterministic conflict-free shard from the current ready frontier, with at most three concurrent tasks.
Ship recomputes readiness after every state transition or integration instead of trusting fixed waves or list order.
No-ready states report exact blockers, invalid state, active work, or completion.
Each selected task receives a bounded transient code/test neighborhood before editing.
Cross-artifact reporting stays read-only; execution remains scoped to the explicitly active slug.

tasks.title: Link evidence and selective invalidation
tasks.description: Ship and verify record attempt-scoped evidence, stale affected descendants, and preserve unrelated ancestors before final integration gates.
acceptance_criteria: Passed version-2 nodes point to current-attempt progress, verification, review, or commit evidence.
Failed or changed upstream nodes block pending descendants and stale passed descendants.
Ancestors reopen only when evidence attributes the cause or their produced output changed.
Blocked descendants return to pending only after every dependency passes; stale nodes require explicit re-execution or verification.
All graph behavior and policy tests pass together without restoring deleted or unrelated files.
